I've noted those for the next round: **more sort orders and a chosen default**, **paging/how many show at once**, and **adjustable text size** — with today's newest-first order and full-content wrapping standing as they are now.

That completes our exploration. Here's everything we've settled, in plain terms:

1. **Quick save** with the page's details (title, description, icon, preview) filled in automatically — and it saves even when a page can't be read, so you never lose a link.
2. **No duplicates** — saving a link you already have takes you to it instead.
3. **Edit** a bookmark's title, address, and description; **odd input is politely refused**.
4. **Tags** — several per bookmark, with suggestions so you reuse them, and a filter that narrows to items carrying *all* the tags you pick.
5. **Search** — quick everyday search across everything, plus a powerful mode (`#tag`, `"exact phrases"`, `AND/OR/NOT`, brackets) that safely falls back if mistyped.
6. **Personal notes** in simple Markdown, kept separate from the page's own description, and searchable.
7. **Read tracking** — "To read" vs "Read" as its own status, with focus views.
8. **Archive** — tuck things away out of the main list but keep them, fully reversible.
9. **Delete** — permanent, deliberate, and confirmed — clearly distinct from archive.
10. **Comfortable on phone and desktop**, with long content wrapping rather than being cut off.

So ten feature areas are settled and their boundary situations explored. **May I now go ahead and build this scope for real?** (The sort/paging/text-size items and the by-website view will wait for the next round.)
